source.title: The Way to Wealth
source.author: Benjamin Franklin
source.summary: A short classic built from Poor Richard's maxims about work, frugality, debt, time, and practical prudence.
source.corePromise: Teach the economic value of industry, restraint, time, and thrift.

target.positioning: a compact wealth discipline book for freelancers, founders, creators, and high-income people who still leak money

us.evidence: Published in 1758 and available as a public-domain Project Gutenberg text.

subtitleOptions: Benjamin Franklin's Money Rules Rebuilt for Freelancers, Founders, and Creators
A Practical Guide to Time, Thrift, Work, Debt, and Durable Wealth
Old Money Discipline for the Subscription Economy
adaptation.modernWorld: Subscription creep, creator income, freelance cash flow, startup salaries, consumer debt, lifestyle inflation, and the hidden cost of wasted attention
toneRules: Keep the aphoristic bite but make the examples modern and concrete.
Use humor sparingly to expose financial self-deception.
Make thrift feel like power and optionality, not smallness.
prohibitedChanges: Do not turn the book into austerity theater.
Do not imply Benjamin Franklin wrote the adaptation.
Do not ignore Franklin's satirical frame when modernizing the message.
coreLessons: Small leaks compound into large losses.
Debt transfers future freedom to someone else.
Industry creates options when paired with restraint.
Frugality is a form of control.
A person who wastes attention wastes earning power.

chapterPlan.title: Father Abraham Joins the Group Chat
chapterPlan.focus: Recreate the original public sermon as modern money advice delivered to ambitious but financially scattered workers.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: A group of founders, freelancers, and creators ask why income keeps disappearing.

chapterPlan.title: Time Is Not Money. Time Is Better.
chapterPlan.focus: Translate Franklin's time discipline into modern attention economics.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Calendars, phones, notification debt, and work that never becomes output.

chapterPlan.title: The Subscription Tax
chapterPlan.focus: Modernize thrift through recurring expenses and lifestyle drift.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: SaaS tools, apps, food delivery, car payments, and status purchases.

chapterPlan.title: The Future Sends an Invoice
chapterPlan.focus: Show debt as a claim on future freedom.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Credit cards, business debt, student loans, and buy-now-pay-later behavior.

chapterPlan.title: Industry Without Leakage
chapterPlan.focus: Pair earning power with cash retention.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: High income only matters when a portion survives.

chapterPlan.title: The Wealth Nobody Claps For
chapterPlan.focus: Make quiet financial strength more desirable than visible spending.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Emergency funds, low burn, skill growth, and strategic patience.

marketingAngles: Benjamin Franklin's thrift classic rebuilt for modern cash flow
